cells.tense: The choosing is happening right now, here, and you're the one holding the pen.
cells.ask: Name one thing you're steering this month, say it to one person, and say what you're letting slide to keep steering it.
cells.core:
When it's going well, you can see how the pieces of something fit, and you use that view to actually pick. This, not that. Said plainly, on purpose, without having to talk yourself into it. Nothing is dragging you by the collar, and nothing is taking your whole arm to hold. The direction is yours and the moment is the one you're standing in.

That combination is rarer than it sounds, and it costs something to keep. So pick one thing you're steering this month, say it out loud to a person who asks, and say what you're letting slide to keep steering it. Keep naming the trade and the grip stays clean.

cells.tense: You're already living a few moves ahead of the present, forcing a shape that hasn't arrived yet.
cells.ask: Pick the one outcome you're gripping. Leave it alone today. Then say out loud what you saw that told you it needed gripping.
cells.core:
You've got a clean view of how the whole thing runs, and the view has turned into a tool for steering events that haven't happened. You're out ahead of the present, pushing an outcome into being before it's ready, and you're doing it with a confidence that comes from seeing the pattern. The trouble is that seeing how something works isn't the same as being there when it does.

The shape you're forcing is bending around the grip. So pick the one outcome you can't put down. Leave it alone today, all day, and let it do what it does without your hand on it. Later, name what you saw that told you it needed gripping. Recognition, without having to close anything.

cells.tense: You're standing at a doorway that's already behind you, and it's still deciding what you can want.
cells.ask: Say one thing you'd like next, out loud, then take one small step toward it today before the feeling arrives.
cells.core:
When it works, the pattern comes back as a map. You can look at how something is put together and it tells you where to put your weight next. The view doesn't have to move you; it just has to show you the next inch. Choosing shows up as the ordinary thing it is — one small yes, then another, not a verdict about what kind of person you are.

What's happening instead is that the reading is still running, but it lands as a reason not to bother. So find one small thing you'd like next. Not the plan. The inch. Say it out loud, and take the step today, before you feel like it. Appetite usually catches up after the walking starts.

cells.tense: You're already writing this page, but you're describing the ink as something that happened to you.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you'd tell a stranger just happened. Then say out loud what you did that made it that way.
cells.core:
Here's the shape when it's owned: you can read how something is put together, and you can also feel your own hand in it. You know which move was yours. There's no drama about it — it's just true that some things got built because you kept showing up, and some because you stopped. The direction is real either way, and you get to say so.

Whatever is steering now is the same thing, uncredited. Moves get made and filed under how things go. Pick one thing you'd tell a stranger just happened, and find the move you made that put it there. One move. Say it out loud, quietly, and let that be enough tonight.
